combos.label: Caution

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is cautious: Jammu and Kashmir GST collections fell -10.6% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, with the latest month down -29.4% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), while electricity demand slipped -0.5% Apr-to-date against India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026). Bank credit still grew +11.2% YoY to Rs 116,297 Cr with a 56.9% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so lending is expanding into a contracting tax and power base.
sector_risks: Demand and output contraction: GST collections -10.6% Apr-to-date and latest month -29.4% YoY (GSTN, to Sep-2026) point to falling turnover and weaker repayment capacity across state industry.
Power availability and usage: electricity demand -0.5% Apr-to-date versus India +9.5% (CEA, to Aug-2026) signals lower operating activity and possible unit closures flagged in the credit lens.
Payment cycles: with credit up +11.2% YoY to Rs 116,297 Cr (RBI, end-Mar-2025) while GST receipts fall, delayed payments and stretched debtor days are the key stress channel.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend: compare trailing 12-month reported turnover against bank credit summations, flagging any gap where credit growth exceeds declared turnover.
Debtor days versus 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90.
Electricity bills trend versus last year: pull 12 months of utility bills and check whether consumption is flat or falling against the state's -0.5% Apr-to-date demand (CEA, to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: An upgrade would need J&K GST collections turning positive against the -10.6% Apr-to-date and -29.4% latest-month readings, and electricity demand recovering from -0.5% toward India's +9.5%.

local_view.why: State GST -10.6% and power demand -0.5% lag India's +6.1% and +9.5%.

brief.verdict_rationale: Punjab's GST collections grew +9.7% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month at +17.6% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and all-bank credit stands at Rs 410,319 Cr, +9.1% YoY with a 58.5% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so demand and credit penetration support the sector. However, electricity demand grew only +8.8% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), and the latest month's +27.8% YoY is a volatile spike rather than a trend, so the call is in line rather than better.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: LUB reports prolonged delays in PMEGP subsidy disbursement for cases approved in 2022, with entrepreneurs bearing bank loan interest while awaiting payment, which can erode working capital and repayment capacity.

Power availability: the credit lens flags power availability as a driver, and LUB cites unscheduled power cuts; CEA shows Punjab electricity demand +8.8% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (data to Aug-2026), so output growth may lag national momentum.
Policy inconsistency and unit closures: LUB raises policy inconsistencies affecting the business environment, a stress factor the credit lens links to unit closures and delayed payments.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The single LUB article (2026-10-08) adds borrower-level detail beyond the data: PMEGP subsidy delays since 2022 approvals, unscheduled power cuts, and law-and-order and policy-inconsistency concerns raised with the Punjab Governor.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend vs bank credit summations: reconcile declared GST turnover against credit account turnover for the last 12 months to detect under-reporting or diversion.
Debtor days vs 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, with no concentration in government or subsidy-linked receivables.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare monthly power bills for the last 12 months against the prior year to confirm production is rising in line with the +8.8% Apr-to-date state demand growth (CEA, data to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move to Better requires Punjab electricity demand Apr-to-date growth to exceed India's +9.5% (currently +8.8%, CEA data to Aug-2026); a move to Worse would be GST growth Apr-to-date falling below India's +6.1% (currently +9.7%, GSTN data to Sep-2026).

local_view.why: GST growth beats India but power demand lags; subsidy delays pressure MSME cash flow.

combos.message: OK to lend: national 100 x 0.6 + local 75 x 0.4 = 90.

reasons.text: Punjab: GST collections +9.7% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% (3.6 pp faster than India) — a local tailwind. [GSTN state-wise GST collections, data to Sep-2026]
India-wide: IIP NIC 29 output +25.2% YoY. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]
India-wide: Output +19.2% Apr-to-date. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]

brief.verdict_rationale: Punjab's GST collections grew +9.7% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month at +17.6% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and all-bank credit stands at Rs 410,319 Cr, +9.1% YoY with a 58.5% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so demand and credit penetration support the sector. However, electricity demand grew only +8.8% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), and the latest month's +27.8% YoY is a volatile spike rather than a trend, so the call is in line rather than better.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: LUB reports prolonged delays in PMEGP subsidy disbursement for cases approved in 2022, with entrepreneurs bearing bank loan interest while awaiting payment, which can erode working capital and repayment capacity.

Power availability: the credit lens flags power availability as a driver, and LUB cites unscheduled power cuts; CEA shows Punjab electricity demand +8.8% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (data to Aug-2026), so output growth may lag national momentum.
Policy inconsistency and unit closures: LUB raises policy inconsistencies affecting the business environment, a stress factor the credit lens links to unit closures and delayed payments.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The single LUB article (2026-10-08) adds borrower-level detail beyond the data: PMEGP subsidy delays since 2022 approvals, unscheduled power cuts, and law-and-order and policy-inconsistency concerns raised with the Punjab Governor.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend vs bank credit summations: reconcile declared GST turnover against credit account turnover for the last 12 months to detect under-reporting or diversion.
Debtor days vs 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, with no concentration in government or subsidy-linked receivables.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare monthly power bills for the last 12 months against the prior year to confirm production is rising in line with the +8.8% Apr-to-date state demand growth (CEA, data to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move to Better requires Punjab electricity demand Apr-to-date growth to exceed India's +9.5% (currently +8.8%, CEA data to Aug-2026); a move to Worse would be GST growth Apr-to-date falling below India's +6.1% (currently +9.7%, GSTN data to Sep-2026).

local_view.why: GST growth beats India but power demand lags; subsidy delays pressure MSME cash flow.

brief.verdict_rationale: State-level demand signals support the MSME book: Uttar Pradesh GST collections rose +14.2% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month +18.2% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and all-bank credit stood at Rs 1,031,463 Cr, +11.6% YoY with a 50.9% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). Net call is constructive on revenue visibility but selective on working-capital-heavy borrowers, given the Noida apparel unit shrinkage reported in the news.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the Muzaffarnagar IIA report says MSME suppliers are treated as ordinary creditors behind larger buyers in insolvency, so a single large-buyer default can freeze a small unit's working capital.

Power-cost and availability risk: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so energy-intensive units face cost pressure without a state demand premium to absorb it.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. borrower_checks: GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credits in the account; investigate any gap where bank credits exceed GST turnover, since UP GST is running +14.2% Apr-to-date (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).

Debtor days vs 90: compute receivables divided by daily sales from the latest filed accounts and GST returns; require debtor days at or below 90, with no single buyer above 25% of receivables given the IIA insolvency-priority complaint.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: obtain 12 months of electricity bills and compare YoY; require bill growth no faster than the +10.0% YoY latest-month state demand figure (CEA, data to Aug-2026), with no arrears or disconnection notices.
brief.change_the_call: A move to UP GST growth below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or UP electricity demand growth falling below the +8.6% Apr-to-date print (CEA, data to Aug-2026), would shift the call to negative; credit growth holding at +11.6% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio at 50.9% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) keeps it constructive.

brief.verdict_rationale: State-level demand signals support the MSME book: Uttar Pradesh GST collections rose +14.2% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month +18.2% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and all-bank credit stood at Rs 1,031,463 Cr, +11.6% YoY with a 50.9% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). The offset is power: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so the state is not outgrowing the national grid. Net call is constructive on revenue visibility but selective on working-capital-heavy borrowers, given the Noida apparel unit shrinkage reported in the news.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the Muzaffarnagar IIA report says MSME suppliers are treated as ordinary creditors behind larger buyers in insolvency, so a single large-buyer default can freeze a small unit's working capital.

Demand/closure risk in export-linked clusters: the news reports Noida apparel units shrinking to 1,800 from 2,400 over the past six months and Noida apparel exports expected to decline to about ₹42,000 crore this financial year from ₹48,000 crore in 2025-26.

Power-cost and availability risk: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so energy-intensive units face cost pressure without a state demand premium to absorb it.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The Noida apparel article is the only current, on-topic item and adds cluster-level closure data (units down to 1,800 from 2,400 in six months) that the state aggregates do not show; the Muzaffarnagar IIA item adds supplier-priority concerns in insolvency, while the Etawah textile video is an old demonetisation report and is not usable as current evidence.
borrower_checks: GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credits in the account; investigate any gap where bank credits exceed GST turnover, since UP GST is running +14.2% Apr-to-date (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).

Debtor days vs 90: compute receivables divided by daily sales from the latest filed accounts and GST returns; require debtor days at or below 90, with no single buyer above 25% of receivables given the IIA insolvency-priority complaint.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: obtain 12 months of electricity bills and compare YoY; require bill growth no faster than the +10.0% YoY latest-month state demand figure (CEA, data to Aug-2026), with no arrears or disconnection notices.
brief.change_the_call: A move to UP GST growth below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or UP electricity demand growth falling below the +8.6% Apr-to-date print (CEA, data to Aug-2026), would shift the call to negative; credit growth holding at +11.6% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio at 50.9% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) keeps it constructive.

local_view.why: UP GST +14.2% vs India +6.1% and credit +11.6% YoY outpace national momentum.

The offset is power: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so the state is not outgrowing the national grid. Net call is constructive on revenue visibility but selective on working-capital-heavy borrowers, given the Noida apparel unit shrinkage reported in the news.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the Muzaffarnagar IIA report says MSME suppliers are treated as ordinary creditors behind larger buyers in insolvency, so a single large-buyer default can freeze a small unit's working capital.

Demand/closure risk in export-linked clusters: the news reports Noida apparel units shrinking to 1,800 from 2,400 over the past six months and Noida apparel exports expected to decline to about ₹42,000 crore this financial year from ₹48,000 crore in 2025-26.

Power-cost and availability risk: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so energy-intensive units face cost pressure without a state demand premium to absorb it.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The Noida apparel article is the only current, on-topic item and adds cluster-level closure data (units down to 1,800 from 2,400 in six months) that the state aggregates do not show; the Muzaffarnagar IIA item adds supplier-priority concerns in insolvency, while the Etawah textile video is an old demonetisation report and is not usable as current evidence.
borrower_checks: GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credits in the account; investigate any gap where bank credits exceed GST turnover, since UP GST is running +14.2% Apr-to-date (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).

Debtor days vs 90: compute receivables divided by daily sales from the latest filed accounts and GST returns; require debtor days at or below 90, with no single buyer above 25% of receivables given the IIA insolvency-priority complaint.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: obtain 12 months of electricity bills and compare YoY; require bill growth no faster than the +10.0% YoY latest-month state demand figure (CEA, data to Aug-2026), with no arrears or disconnection notices.
brief.change_the_call: A move to UP GST growth below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or UP electricity demand growth falling below the +8.6% Apr-to-date print (CEA, data to Aug-2026), would shift the call to negative; credit growth holding at +11.6% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio at 50.9% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) keeps it constructive.

brief.verdict_rationale: State-level demand signals support the MSME book: Uttar Pradesh GST collections rose +14.2% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month +18.2% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and all-bank credit stood at Rs 1,031,463 Cr, +11.6% YoY with a 50.9% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). The offset is power: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so the state is not outgrowing the national grid. Net call is constructive on revenue visibility but selective on working-capital-heavy borrowers, given the Noida apparel unit shrinkage reported in the news.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the Muzaffarnagar IIA report says MSME suppliers are treated as ordinary creditors behind larger buyers in insolvency, so a single large-buyer default can freeze a small unit's working capital.

Demand/closure risk in export-linked clusters: the news reports Noida apparel units shrinking to 1,800 from 2,400 over the past six months and Noida apparel exports expected to decline to about ₹42,000 crore this financial year from ₹48,000 crore in 2025-26.

Power-cost and availability risk: UP electricity demand grew +8.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% and +10.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so energy-intensive units face cost pressure without a state demand premium to absorb it.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The Noida apparel article is the only current, on-topic item and adds cluster-level closure data (units down to 1,800 from 2,400 in six months) that the state aggregates do not show; the Muzaffarnagar IIA item adds supplier-priority concerns in insolvency, while the Etawah textile video is an old demonetisation report and is not usable as current evidence.
borrower_checks: GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credits in the account; investigate any gap where bank credits exceed GST turnover, since UP GST is running +14.2% Apr-to-date (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).

Debtor days vs 90: compute receivables divided by daily sales from the latest filed accounts and GST returns; require debtor days at or below 90, with no single buyer above 25% of receivables given the IIA insolvency-priority complaint.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: obtain 12 months of electricity bills and compare YoY; require bill growth no faster than the +10.0% YoY latest-month state demand figure (CEA, data to Aug-2026), with no arrears or disconnection notices.
brief.change_the_call: A move to UP GST growth below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or UP electricity demand growth falling below the +8.6% Apr-to-date print (CEA, data to Aug-2026), would shift the call to negative; credit growth holding at +11.6% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio at 50.9% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) keeps it constructive.

local_view.why: UP GST +14.2% vs India +6.1% and credit +11.6% YoY outpace national momentum.

brief.verdict_rationale: Sikkim's GST collections fell -53.8% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, with the latest month at -51.0% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand fell -0.5% Apr-to-date versus India +9.5%, latest month -5.1% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026). Against this contracting state demand, all-bank credit still grew +8.4% YoY to Rs 7,136 Cr with a credit-deposit ratio of 43.4% (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so lending is expanding into a shrinking tax and power base. The call is negative for Sikkim industry MSME exposure until GST and electricity trends stop diverging from India.
sector_risks: Demand and output contraction: GST collections -53.8% Apr-to-date and latest month -51.0% YoY (GSTN, to Sep-2026) point to falling turnover and unit closures among MSME borrowers.

Power availability and usage: electricity demand -0.5% Apr-to-date and -5.1% YoY latest month (CEA, to Aug-2026) versus India +9.5%, consistent with reduced operating activity and weaker electricity bill trends.

Payment cycles and delayed payments: credit of Rs 7,136 Cr growing +8.4% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025) while state GST falls implies receivables building; the credit lens flags debtor days versus 90 as the stress marker.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The only relevant item is the Sikkim government welcoming the MSME Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 (Sikkimexpress, Aug 13, 2026), which signals policy support but adds no turnover, payment or closure data beyond the pack.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend: compare borrower's GST-reported turnover for Apr-Sep 2026 against the state's -53.8% Apr-to-date and -51.0% latest-month YoY (GSTN, to Sep-2026); require the borrower to be no worse than the state figure.
Debtor days versus 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, with no increase versus the prior year.

Electricity bills trend versus last year: pull 12 months of utility bills and compare YoY against the state's -5.1% latest-month and -0.5% Apr-to-date demand figures (CEA, to Aug-2026); a steeper fall signals reduced operations.
brief.change_the_call: A reversal to positive Sikkim GST growth (Apr-to-date turning above 0% versus the current -53.8%) and electricity demand growth returning above 0% (from -0.5% Apr-to-date) would move the call from negative toward neutral.

local_view.why: State GST -53.8% and power demand -0.5% versus India +6.1% and +9.5%.

sector_risks: Demand and output risk: electricity demand at -0.6% Apr-to-date and -1.7% YoY latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026) points to weaker state activity than the India +9.5% trend, which pressures MSME volumes and repayment capacity.

Payment-cycle risk: with all-bank credit at Rs 10,653 Cr, +17.4% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025), receivables build-up can outpace turnover; the credit lens flags delayed payments and debtor days above 90 as stress markers.

Tax-collection divergence risk: GST at +11.1% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% (GSTN, data to Sep-2026) is a positive, but the -0.6% power demand signal means reported turnover may not translate into cash flow, raising unit-closure risk.

borrower_checks: GST turnover reconciliation: compare 12-month GST returns against bank credit summations, flagging any gap above 10% of declared turnover.
Debtor days: obtain the receivables ageing and require debtor days at or below 90, consistent with the credit lens benchmark.
Electricity bills trend: compare the last 12 months of power bills against the prior year, given state demand at -0.6% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move to positive electricity demand growth (above 0% Apr-to-date, versus -0.6% now) alongside GST growth holding above India's +6.1% would upgrade the call; a fall in GST growth below India's rate or credit growth slowing from +17.4% YoY would downgrade it.

brief.verdict_rationale: Manipur electricity demand is growing faster than the national trend (+12.6% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5%, and +22.1% YoY in the latest month, CEA data to Aug-2026), pointing to real operating activity rather than a contracting industrial base. All-bank credit of Rs 13,396 Cr grew +10.3% YoY with a credit-deposit ratio of 76.6% (RBI state handbook, end-Mar-2025), so leverage is expanding but not stretched against deposits. The call is a cautious positive on operating demand, with repayment risk resting on payment cycles rather than volume.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments as a core stress driver, and with credit at Rs 13,396 Cr (+10.3% YoY, end-Mar-2025) growing alongside demand, receivables rather than sales are the likely fault line.

Power-cost and availability risk: the lens lists power availability as a driver, and the +22.1% YoY latest-month demand surge (CEA, to Aug-2026) can translate into tariffs, load restrictions or captive-generation costs that squeeze unit margins.

Unit closures and tax-collection lag: the lens names tax collections lagging India and unit closures as stress signals; the pack has no GST or closure data, so this risk is currently unmeasured and must be tested at borrower level.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage.
borrower_checks: GST turnover for the last 12 months reconciled against bank credit summations on the account, with any gap between reported turnover and credit flows explained in writing.
Debtor days calculated from the sales ledger, benchmarked at 90 days, with the ageing profile of receivables above 90 days listed by counterparty.
Electricity bills for the last 12 months compared month-by-month against the prior year, checking that consumption growth is consistent with reported output.
brief.change_the_call: A fall in Manipur electricity demand growth below the India +9.5% benchmark, or all-bank credit growth dropping below the current +10.3% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio moving away from 76.6%, would shift the call to negative.

local_view.why: State power demand growth of +12.6% outpaces India's +9.5%, signalling above-average activity.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is to lend selectively: Assam's GST collections rose +36.9% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, and the latest month was +87.6% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), while all-bank credit reached Rs 154,473 Cr, +15.6% YoY, with a 62.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). The offset is weak power demand, +1.9% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% and +8.8% in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), which points to uneven operating activity behind the tax surge.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and with all-bank credit at Rs 154,473 Cr, +15.6% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025), receivables quality rather than demand is the main repayment risk.

Output and power-use divergence: Assam electricity demand grew only +1.9% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so units may be running below capacity even where GST turnover is rising.
Tax-collection volatility: the latest month's +87.6% YoY GST jump (GSTN, data to Sep-2026) is far above the +36.9% Apr-to-date pace, so a single strong month should not be read as a durable trend.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend over the last 12 months versus bank credit summations, benchmarked to the state's +36.9% Apr-to-date GST growth (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).
Debtor days versus 90, with an ageing split of receivables beyond 90 days.
Electricity bills for the last 12 months versus the prior year, benchmarked to Assam's +1.9% Apr-to-date demand growth (CEA, data to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move to a more cautious stance would follow Assam electricity demand growth staying below India's +9.5% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026) or GST growth falling below the +6.1% India Apr-to-date pace (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).

local_view.why: State GST growth of +36.9% far outpaces India's +6.1%.

brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. borrower_checks: Debtor days versus the 90-day benchmark, reconciled to the 210-day dispute timeline in the news; flag any receivable ageing beyond 90 days.

brief.change_the_call: An upgrade would need Chhattisgarh GST growth closing the gap to India's +6.1% and latest-month electricity demand turning positive from -8.7% YoY; a fall in credit growth below the +15.3% YoY pace with credit-deposit ratio easing from 79.5% would harden the cautious stance.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is cautious: Chhattisgarh GST collections grew only +2.4% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, and the latest month was just +0.8% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), while electricity demand fell -8.7% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026). Against this, all-bank credit is Rs 223,098 Cr, +15.3% YoY with a 79.5% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so credit is expanding faster than the tax and power signals that would validate it.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the news reports Rs 280.65 crore of MSME payments stuck in disputes across 890 pending cases, with Rs 179.29 crore in 488 cases at application stage and Rs 101.36 crore in 402 under hearing (Bhaskar, 2026-09-04), directly hitting working capital.

Demand and output weakness: latest-month electricity demand -8.7% YoY and GST +0.8% YoY (CEA to Aug-2026; GSTN to Sep-2026) point to softer state activity than the +15.3% YoY credit growth (RBI, end-Mar-2025) implies.

Buyer-concentration and quality-dispute risk: the article names ACC, BSP, Jindal, Simplex and government bodies PWD, PHE, CSIDC and Tourism as buyers withholding payment on quality grounds, so receivables hinge on a few large counterparties.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The one relevant article (Bhaskar, 2026-09-04) adds that 890 payment-dispute cases worth Rs 280.65 crore are pending, that 1,168 cases were heard in 30 meetings between 24 Dec 2024 and 24 Dec 2025, and that a new 210-day dispute process (90 days mediation, 30 days to arbitration, 90 days for award) plus a 15-day written-objection rule is intended to speed recovery.
borrower_checks: Debtor days versus the 90-day benchmark, reconciled to the 210-day dispute timeline in the news; flag any receivable ageing beyond 90 days.
GST turnover trend versus bank credit summations, tested against the state's +2.4% Apr-to-date GST growth (GSTN, to Sep-2026) to confirm the borrower is not outgrowing the state.
Electricity bill trend versus last year, compared with the state's -8.7% YoY latest-month demand (CEA, to Aug-2026), to verify actual operating levels.
brief.change_the_call: An upgrade would need Chhattisgarh GST growth closing the gap to India's +6.1% and latest-month electricity demand turning positive from -8.7% YoY; a fall in credit growth below the +15.3% YoY pace with credit-deposit ratio easing from 79.5% would harden the cautious stance.

local_view.why: State GST +2.4% and power demand -8.7% YoY lag India while credit grows +15.3%.

brief.verdict_rationale: State-level demand signals are strong: Gujarat GST collections rose +11.9% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% with the latest month +17.3% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), electricity demand +11.0% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), and all-bank credit stood at Rs 1,125,894 Cr, +13.2% YoY with a 79.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). The call is therefore constructive on aggregate state demand, but the news flow shows acute, cluster-specific stress in Surat-South Gujarat textiles and power supply that the state aggregates do not capture.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: articles report delayed buyer payments and unsold inventory squeezing working capital in Surat weaving units, which sits against the pack's +13.2% YoY credit growth (RBI, end-Mar-2025) — credit is expanding faster than the cash conversion the news describes.

Input-cost and margin risk: yarn prices up 40% to 45% since June with weak fabric demand (Apparel Views/Textile Value Chain, 2026-10-15) threatens unit closures and early Diwali shutdowns, the stress the credit lens flags as 'unit closures'.

Power-availability risk: eight-hour shutdowns from 4 PM to midnight on staggering holidays affecting more than 250 units in Navsari GIDC (New Indian Express, 2026-10-18) conflict with the pack's +11.5% YoY latest-month electricity demand (CEA, to Aug-2026) — demand is rising while supply is being rationed.
brief.local_news: Local coverage adds cluster-level stress the state aggregates miss: an eight-hour power shutdown directive hitting more than 250 units in Navsari GIDC and threatening losses of thousands of crores (New Indian Express, 2026-10-18), and Surat weavers facing 40% to 45% yarn price rises since June with possible loom closures about 15 days early (Apparel Views and Textile Value Chain, 2026-10-15). Both point to delayed payments and liquidity pressure concentrated in MSMEs.
borrower_checks: Debtor days vs 90: obtain the borrower's latest receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, given reported buyer payment delays in Surat textiles.
GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credit summations to confirm credit growth is matched by declared sales, not inventory build-up.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare the last 6-12 months of electricity bills against the same months last year to verify actual operating hours and output, given the 4 PM-to-midnight shutdown directive.
brief.change_the_call: A reversal would follow Gujarat GST growth falling below India's +6.1% or electricity demand growth falling below India's +9.5% on the Apr-to-date basis, or credit growth dropping below the current +13.2% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio moving off 79.7%.

local_view.why: State demand beats India, but power cuts and 40-45% yarn inflation hit MSME cash flow.

Gujarat Textile Industry Faces Possible Early Diwali Shutdown Amid 45% Yarn Price Rise

combos.label: Caution
combos.message: Caution: national 48 x 0.6 + local 75 x 0.4 = 59.

reasons.text: Gujarat: GST collections +11.9% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% (5.8 pp faster than India) — a local tailwind. [GSTN state-wise GST collections, data to Sep-2026]
India-wide: Exports +32.5% Apr-to-date in USD (Rs 10,743 Cr FYTD). [Dept of Commerce, data to Sep-2026]
India-wide: Bank credit +26.8% YoY vs output +3.8% (gap +23.0 pp). [RBI bank credit vs output, data to Aug-2026]

brief.verdict_rationale: State-level demand signals are strong: Gujarat GST collections rose +11.9% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% with the latest month +17.3% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), electricity demand +11.0% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), and all-bank credit stood at Rs 1,125,894 Cr, +13.2% YoY with a 79.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). The call is therefore constructive on aggregate state demand, but the news flow shows acute, cluster-specific stress in Surat-South Gujarat textiles and power supply that the state aggregates do not capture.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle risk: articles report delayed buyer payments and unsold inventory squeezing working capital in Surat weaving units, which sits against the pack's +13.2% YoY credit growth (RBI, end-Mar-2025) — credit is expanding faster than the cash conversion the news describes.

Input-cost and margin risk: yarn prices up 40% to 45% since June with weak fabric demand (Apparel Views/Textile Value Chain, 2026-10-15) threatens unit closures and early Diwali shutdowns, the stress the credit lens flags as 'unit closures'.

Power-availability risk: eight-hour shutdowns from 4 PM to midnight on staggering holidays affecting more than 250 units in Navsari GIDC (New Indian Express, 2026-10-18) conflict with the pack's +11.5% YoY latest-month electricity demand (CEA, to Aug-2026) — demand is rising while supply is being rationed.
brief.local_news: Local coverage adds cluster-level stress the state aggregates miss: an eight-hour power shutdown directive hitting more than 250 units in Navsari GIDC and threatening losses of thousands of crores (New Indian Express, 2026-10-18), and Surat weavers facing 40% to 45% yarn price rises since June with possible loom closures about 15 days early (Apparel Views and Textile Value Chain, 2026-10-15). Both point to delayed payments and liquidity pressure concentrated in MSMEs.
borrower_checks: Debtor days vs 90: obtain the borrower's latest receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, given reported buyer payment delays in Surat textiles.
GST turnover vs bank credit summations: reconcile 12-month GST-reported turnover against total bank credit summations to confirm credit growth is matched by declared sales, not inventory build-up.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare the last 6-12 months of electricity bills against the same months last year to verify actual operating hours and output, given the 4 PM-to-midnight shutdown directive.
brief.change_the_call: A reversal would follow Gujarat GST growth falling below India's +6.1% or electricity demand growth falling below India's +9.5% on the Apr-to-date basis, or credit growth dropping below the current +13.2% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio moving off 79.7%.

local_view.why: State demand beats India, but power cuts and 40-45% yarn inflation hit MSME cash flow.

brief.verdict_rationale: Maharashtra's GST collections grew +8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, with the latest month at +15.5% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), signalling state demand running ahead of the national average. However, electricity demand grew only +6.0% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), pointing to softer industrial utilisation than the tax data implies. All-bank credit of Rs 4,483,171 Cr at +11.2% YoY with a 98.1% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows lending is already stretched against deposits, so incremental exposure needs borrower-level evidence rather than sector momentum.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and with the credit-deposit ratio at 98.1% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) banks have little deposit headroom to absorb stretched working-capital cycles.

Power availability and utilisation: electricity demand grew +6.0% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so any borrower whose output depends on grid-heavy operations faces weaker volume support than the GST headline suggests.

Unit closures and tax-base attrition: the credit lens lists unit closures as a stress signal, and the GST growth of +8.6% Apr-to-date versus +6.1% for India (GSTN, data to Sep-2026) may overstate the health of the surviving base if closures are concentrated among smaller filers.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage.
borrower_checks: GST turnover reconciliation: match trailing-12-month GST returns against bank credit summations, and require the ratio to be within 10% before sanction.
Debtor days: confirm collection period is at or below 90 days, per the credit lens benchmark, using the latest audited receivables and ageing schedule.
Electricity bills trend: compare the last 12 months of utility bills against the prior year, and require growth consistent with reported output rather than a decline that signals idle capacity.
brief.change_the_call: A move in Maharashtra electricity demand growth below the current +6.0% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026), or a fall in GST growth below India's +6.1% (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), would shift the call to negative.

All-bank credit of Rs 4,483,171 Cr at +11.2% YoY with a 98.1% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows lending is already stretched against deposits, so incremental exposure needs borrower-level evidence rather than sector momentum.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and with the credit-deposit ratio at 98.1% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) banks have little deposit headroom to absorb stretched working-capital cycles.

Power availability and utilisation: electricity demand grew +6.0% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026), so any borrower whose output depends on grid-heavy operations faces weaker volume support than the GST headline suggests.

Unit closures and tax-base attrition: the credit lens lists unit closures as a stress signal, and the GST growth of +8.6% Apr-to-date versus +6.1% for India (GSTN, data to Sep-2026) may overstate the health of the surviving base if closures are concentrated among smaller filers.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage.
borrower_checks: GST turnover reconciliation: match trailing-12-month GST returns against bank credit summations, and require the ratio to be within 10% before sanction.
Debtor days: confirm collection period is at or below 90 days, per the credit lens benchmark, using the latest audited receivables and ageing schedule.
Electricity bills trend: compare the last 12 months of utility bills against the prior year, and require growth consistent with reported output rather than a decline that signals idle capacity.
brief.change_the_call: A move in Maharashtra electricity demand growth below the current +6.0% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026), or a fall in GST growth below India's +6.1% (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), would shift the call to negative.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is constructive: Karnataka GST collections rose +11.1% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, with the latest month at +15.7% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand grew +23.3% Apr-to-date versus +9.5% nationally, latest month +34.8% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026), showing state activity running ahead of the country. All-bank credit of Rs 1,371,514 Cr at +10.7% YoY with a 67.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows leverage is expanding but still funded by deposits. The offset is cost-side: KASSIA reports a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and strike threats, so repayment capacity depends on power-cost pass-through rather than demand.
sector_risks: Power cost shock: KASSIA cites a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and warns units may cease operations, which sits against the +23.3% Apr-to-date electricity demand growth (CEA, to Aug-2026) — higher volumes at higher unit cost squeeze MSME margins.

Payment and receivables stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments and debtor days versus 90; with all-bank credit at Rs 1,371,514 Cr, +10.7% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025), working-capital borrowing can outrun collections if receivables stretch.

Policy and fiscal friction: the CM ruled out a power charge cut for industries and attributed heavy bills to two months of arrears (news), while the Deputy CM said banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes (news) — both raise refinancing and cash-flow risk for small units.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The extracts are undated KASSIA topic-page items and add two things the data pack lacks: a Rs 2.89 per unit June tariff hike that KASSIA says could force unit closures, and the CM's refusal to cut industrial power charges, with bills inflated by two months of arrears. They also record the Deputy CM's claim that banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes for entrepreneurs.
borrower_checks: GST turnover versus bank credit summations: reconcile trailing-12-month GST returns against total bank debits/credits; flag if bank credit turnover exceeds GST-declared turnover by more than 10%.
Debtor days versus 90: compute receivables over trailing-12-month sales; require at or below 90 days, with any increase over the prior year explained by named customers.

Electricity bills trend versus last year: obtain 12 months of utility bills and compare unit consumption and per-unit cost year-on-year, testing the borrower's exposure to the reported Rs 2.89 per unit June hike.
brief.change_the_call: A reversal to Karnataka GST growth at or below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or electricity demand growth falling to India's +9.5% Apr-to-date (CEA, to Aug-2026), would move the call from constructive to neutral.

local_view.why: State GST +11.1% and power demand +23.3% Apr-to-date both outpace India.

reasons.text: Karnataka: GST collections +11.1% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% (5.0 pp faster than India) — a local tailwind. [GSTN state-wise GST collections, data to Sep-2026]
Karnataka: electricity demand +23.3% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (13.8 pp faster than India) — a local tailwind. [CEA Power Supply Position, data to Aug-2026]
India-wide: IIP NIC 29 output +25.2% YoY. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is constructive: Karnataka GST collections rose +11.1% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, with the latest month at +15.7% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand grew +23.3% Apr-to-date versus +9.5% nationally, latest month +34.8% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026), showing state activity running ahead of the country. All-bank credit of Rs 1,371,514 Cr at +10.7% YoY with a 67.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows leverage is expanding but still funded by deposits. The offset is cost-side: KASSIA reports a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and strike threats, so repayment capacity depends on power-cost pass-through rather than demand.
sector_risks: Power cost shock: KASSIA cites a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and warns units may cease operations, which sits against the +23.3% Apr-to-date electricity demand growth (CEA, to Aug-2026) — higher volumes at higher unit cost squeeze MSME margins.

Payment and receivables stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments and debtor days versus 90; with all-bank credit at Rs 1,371,514 Cr, +10.7% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025), working-capital borrowing can outrun collections if receivables stretch.

Policy and fiscal friction: the CM ruled out a power charge cut for industries and attributed heavy bills to two months of arrears (news), while the Deputy CM said banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes (news) — both raise refinancing and cash-flow risk for small units.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The extracts are undated KASSIA topic-page items and add two things the data pack lacks: a Rs 2.89 per unit June tariff hike that KASSIA says could force unit closures, and the CM's refusal to cut industrial power charges, with bills inflated by two months of arrears. They also record the Deputy CM's claim that banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes for entrepreneurs.
borrower_checks: GST turnover versus bank credit summations: reconcile trailing-12-month GST returns against total bank debits/credits; flag if bank credit turnover exceeds GST-declared turnover by more than 10%.
Debtor days versus 90: compute receivables over trailing-12-month sales; require at or below 90 days, with any increase over the prior year explained by named customers.

Electricity bills trend versus last year: obtain 12 months of utility bills and compare unit consumption and per-unit cost year-on-year, testing the borrower's exposure to the reported Rs 2.89 per unit June hike.
brief.change_the_call: A reversal to Karnataka GST growth at or below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or electricity demand growth falling to India's +9.5% Apr-to-date (CEA, to Aug-2026), would move the call from constructive to neutral.

local_view.why: State GST +11.1% and power demand +23.3% Apr-to-date both outpace India.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is constructive: Karnataka GST collections rose +11.1% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, with the latest month at +15.7% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand grew +23.3% Apr-to-date versus +9.5% nationally, latest month +34.8% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026), showing state activity running ahead of the country. All-bank credit of Rs 1,371,514 Cr at +10.7% YoY with a 67.7% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows leverage is expanding but still funded by deposits. The offset is cost-side: KASSIA reports a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and strike threats, so repayment capacity depends on power-cost pass-through rather than demand.
sector_risks: Power cost shock: KASSIA cites a Rs 2.89 per unit tariff hike for June and warns units may cease operations, which sits against the +23.3% Apr-to-date electricity demand growth (CEA, to Aug-2026) — higher volumes at higher unit cost squeeze MSME margins.

Payment and receivables stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments and debtor days versus 90; with all-bank credit at Rs 1,371,514 Cr, +10.7% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025), working-capital borrowing can outrun collections if receivables stretch.

Policy and fiscal friction: the CM ruled out a power charge cut for industries and attributed heavy bills to two months of arrears (news), while the Deputy CM said banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes (news) — both raise refinancing and cash-flow risk for small units.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The extracts are undated KASSIA topic-page items and add two things the data pack lacks: a Rs 2.89 per unit June tariff hike that KASSIA says could force unit closures, and the CM's refusal to cut industrial power charges, with bills inflated by two months of arrears. They also record the Deputy CM's claim that banks are not supporting central collateral-free loan schemes for entrepreneurs.

brief.verdict_rationale: State demand signals are ahead of India: Kerala GST collections rose +10.3% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% and latest month +10.6% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), with electricity demand +11.1% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026). But all-bank credit of Rs 633,196 Cr at +9.0% YoY with a 68.8% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows credit already tracking demand, so the call is in line rather than better.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: news reports cardamom export payment cycles stretching from the usual 15 days to over a month and Gulf shipment clearance of 60 to 70 days, a cash-flow crunch in a Rs 4,500 crore industry (Tridge, 2026-10-30).

Power reliability: news reports 20 to 30 percent production declines from power cuts and generator diesel costs of about Rs 1 lakh per month for a 350 kVA set (Deshabhimani, 2026-09-23), despite state electricity demand growing +11.1% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026).

Input-cost and working-capital squeeze: news cites West Asia conflict raising raw material prices and cardamom prices above Rs 3,000 per kilogram lifting working capital needs (Tridge, 2026-10-30; Deshabhimani, 2026-09-23).
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The two articles add unit-level stress not visible in the aggregates: power cuts cutting output 20 to 30 percent and generator diesel at about Rs 1 lakh per month (Deshabhimani, 2026-09-23), and export payment cycles extending from 15 days to over a month with 60 to 70 day Gulf clearance (Tridge, 2026-10-30).
borrower_checks: Debtor days vs 90, with export receivables aged against the reported 60 to 70 day Gulf clearance cycle.
GST turnover vs bank credit summations, reconciled to the state's +10.3% Apr-to-date GST growth (GSTN, data to Sep-2026).
Electricity bills trend vs last year, checked against the state's +11.1% Apr-to-date demand growth (CEA, data to Aug-2026) and any generator diesel spend.
brief.change_the_call: A move in Kerala GST growth below India's +6.1% or electricity demand growth below India's +9.5% (GSTN to Sep-2026; CEA to Aug-2026) would shift the call to worse.

local_view.why: State GST and power demand beat India, but credit at +9.0% already matches.

brief.verdict_rationale: State demand signals are ahead of India: Kerala GST collections rose +10.3% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% and latest month +10.6% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), with electricity demand +11.1% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026). But all-bank credit of Rs 633,196 Cr at +9.0% YoY with a 68.8% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows credit already tracking demand, so the call is in line rather than better.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: news reports cardamom export payment cycles stretching from the usual 15 days to over a month and Gulf shipment clearance of 60 to 70 days, a cash-flow crunch in a Rs 4,500 crore industry (Tridge, 2026-10-30).

Power reliability: news reports 20 to 30 percent production declines from power cuts and generator diesel costs of about Rs 1 lakh per month for a 350 kVA set (Deshabhimani, 2026-09-23), despite state electricity demand growing +11.1% Apr-to-date (CEA, data to Aug-2026).

Input-cost and working-capital squeeze: news cites West Asia conflict raising raw material prices and cardamom prices above Rs 3,000 per kilogram lifting working capital needs (Tridge, 2026-10-30; Deshabhimani, 2026-09-23).
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. brief.verdict_rationale: The call is negative: Tamil Nadu GST collections fell -3.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, and the latest month was -4.5% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), showing state tax turnover contracting while all-bank credit grew +11.4% YoY to Rs 1,762,746 Cr with a credit-deposit ratio of 115.4% (RBI, end-Mar-2025). Electricity demand of +9.8% Apr-to-date and +12.2% YoY latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026) is not translating into GST turnover, so credit is outrunning the revenue base that services it.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle and unit-closure stress: news reports over 50% of Tiruppur knitwear units already shut, with the remainder at risk, against GST collections of -3.2% Apr-to-date and -4.5% YoY latest month (GSTN, to Sep-2026).

Cost and margin squeeze: news reports production costs up more than 50% on yarn and dyeing charges, plus indirect power tariff increases, which pressures repayment capacity even as all-bank credit stands at Rs 1,762,746 Cr, +11.4% YoY (RBI, end-Mar-2025).

Concentration and leverage: a credit-deposit ratio of 115.4% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) leaves little deposit cushion, while news reports over 90% of Tiruppur firms are MSMEs employing about 10 lakh workers, so a cluster shock hits many small exposures at once.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The Tiruppur reports (Hindutamil, apcnewstamil, Dinamalar, 28-29 Oct 2026) add unit-level distress the state aggregates hide: over 50% of knitwear firms reportedly closed, production costs up more than 50%, and a protest planned after 10 Nov 2026. The prison-industries tender of Rs 67 crore (Samayam, 31 Oct 2026) is a state procurement item, not MSME credit evidence.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend: pull 12-month GST returns and compare filed turnover against bank credit summations; require turnover not declining while GST collections run -3.2% Apr-to-date (GSTN, to Sep-2026).
Debtor days vs 90: compute receivables over daily sales from the latest financials and ageing; flag any borrower above 90 days given reported payment delays in the cluster.

Electricity bills trend vs last year: obtain 12 months of power bills and compare unit consumption and per-unit cost year-on-year, testing against state demand of +9.8% Apr-to-date and +12.2% YoY latest month (CEA, to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move to neutral requires Tamil Nadu GST collections turning positive Apr-to-date from -3.2% and the latest month recovering from -4.5% YoY (GSTN, to Sep-2026); a further fall in either figure would harden the negative call.

local_view.why: State GST contracting while credit grows 11.4% and Tiruppur units close.

brief.verdict_rationale: Puducherry's GST collections fell 20.7% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, with the latest month down 30.9% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), while electricity demand grew only 6.1% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% (CEA, data to Aug-2026) — both point to weak state-level activity. Yet all-bank credit still grew 12.1% YoY to Rs 24,561 Cr with a 72.0% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so credit is expanding into a contracting tax base. The call is cautious: lending here is running ahead of the revenue and power signals that normally validate it.
sector_risks: Demand and output contraction: GST collections -20.7% Apr-to-date and -30.9% in the latest month (GSTN, to Sep-2026) signal falling turnover, which erodes the cash flow that services MSME working capital.

Power availability and usage lag: electricity demand +6.1% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5% (CEA, to Aug-2026) is consistent with under-used capacity or unit closures, so fixed-cost absorption and repayment capacity weaken.

Payment-cycle stress: with credit up 12.1% YoY to Rs 24,561 Cr (RBI, end-Mar-2025) while GST receipts fall, receivables may be funded by borrowing rather than collected — delayed payments risk flagged in the credit lens.

borrower_checks: GST turnover trend: compare the borrower's 12-month GST-reported turnover against bank statement credits; require GST turnover to be at least 90% of bank credit summations, and flag any gap above 10%.

brief.verdict_rationale: The state's demand-side indicators are running well ahead of the national benchmark: Telangana GST collections rose +13.8% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month at +18.1% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand grew +15.7% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5%, latest month +19.9% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026). All-bank credit of Rs 1,045,686 Cr at +11.1% YoY with a credit-deposit ratio of 111.6% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows the system is already heavily lent into this expansion, so the call is constructive on demand but selective on working-capital discipline.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the credit-deposit ratio of 111.6% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) means little slack for borrowers whose receivables stretch.

Power reliability and cost: news reports unscheduled power cuts around Hyderabad forcing MSMEs onto expensive diesel gensets, and TGSPDCL discussions covering tariffs and delayed payment surcharges — a direct hit to unit margins despite +15.7% Apr-to-date electricity demand (CEA, to Aug-2026).

Demand reversal risk: the +18.1% YoY latest-month GST growth (GSTN, to Sep-2026) is a single strong print; a fall back toward the India +6.1% rate would leave +11.1% YoY credit growth (RBI, end-Mar-2025) exposed.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. Local coverage adds operational detail the data pack lacks: unscheduled power cuts are pushing Hyderabad-area MSMEs to reinstall and run diesel generators, and TGSPDCL has committed to priority action on supply reliability, tariffs and delayed payment surcharges following a stakeholders' meeting.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend vs bank credit summations: require declared GST turnover growth at or above the state's +13.8% Apr-to-date rate (GSTN, to Sep-2026) and no credit growth outpacing turnover.
Debtor days vs 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days at or below 90.
Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare the last 6 months of power bills and diesel/genset spend against the prior year, given +15.7% Apr-to-date state demand (CEA, to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move in Telangana GST growth from +13.8% Apr-to-date toward the India +6.1% rate, or electricity demand from +15.7% toward India's +9.5% (GSTN to Sep-2026; CEA to Aug-2026), would shift the call to cautious.

local_view.why: State GST +13.8% and power demand +15.7% both outpace India's +6.1% and +9.5%.

India-wide: IIP NIC 23 output +11.4% YoY. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]

brief.verdict_rationale: The state's demand-side indicators are running well ahead of the national benchmark: Telangana GST collections rose +13.8% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1%, with the latest month at +18.1% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), and electricity demand grew +15.7% Apr-to-date vs India +9.5%, latest month +19.9% YoY (CEA, data to Aug-2026). All-bank credit of Rs 1,045,686 Cr at +11.1% YoY with a credit-deposit ratio of 111.6% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) shows the system is already heavily lent into this expansion, so the call is constructive on demand but selective on working-capital discipline.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: the credit lens flags delayed payments, and the credit-deposit ratio of 111.6% (RBI, end-Mar-2025) means little slack for borrowers whose receivables stretch.

Power reliability and cost: news reports unscheduled power cuts around Hyderabad forcing MSMEs onto expensive diesel gensets, and TGSPDCL discussions covering tariffs and delayed payment surcharges — a direct hit to unit margins despite +15.7% Apr-to-date electricity demand (CEA, to Aug-2026).

Demand reversal risk: the +18.1% YoY latest-month GST growth (GSTN, to Sep-2026) is a single strong print; a fall back toward the India +6.1% rate would leave +11.1% YoY credit growth (RBI, end-Mar-2025) exposed.
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. Local coverage adds operational detail the data pack lacks: unscheduled power cuts are pushing Hyderabad-area MSMEs to reinstall and run diesel generators, and TGSPDCL has committed to priority action on supply reliability, tariffs and delayed payment surcharges following a stakeholders' meeting.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend vs bank credit summations: require declared GST turnover growth at or above the state's +13.8% Apr-to-date rate (GSTN, to Sep-2026) and no credit growth outpacing turnover.
Debtor days vs 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days at or below 90.
Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare the last 6 months of power bills and diesel/genset spend against the prior year, given +15.7% Apr-to-date state demand (CEA, to Aug-2026).
brief.change_the_call: A move in Telangana GST growth from +13.8% Apr-to-date toward the India +6.1% rate, or electricity demand from +15.7% toward India's +9.5% (GSTN to Sep-2026; CEA to Aug-2026), would shift the call to cautious.

local_view.why: State GST +13.8% and power demand +15.7% both outpace India's +6.1% and +9.5%.

A.P. Chambers seeks CM’s intervention for release of ₹5,000 crore of industrial incentives

combos.label: Not enough sector data
combos.message: Not enough verified national data for Telecommunications — Unknown — collect.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is cautious: AP GST collections fell -0.2% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1% (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), showing state tax turnover lagging the national trend, while all-bank credit stands at Rs 832,527 Cr, +9.0% YoY with a credit-deposit ratio of 151.1% (RBI, end-Mar-2025), meaning lending is already stretched relative to deposits. Offsetting this, electricity demand rose +18.1% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% and +23.0% YoY in the latest month (CEA, data to Aug-2026), indicating real activity, but the ₹5,000 Cr incentive backlog reported in October 2026 is a direct cash-flow drag on MSME repayment capacity.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle stress: AP Chambers reports roughly ₹5,000 crore in pending MSME and food-processing incentives, with only around ₹1,000 crore released the previous year, and states the delays have affected borrowers' ability to repay loans (news, Oct-2026).

Revenue/activity divergence: GST collections at -0.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% (GSTN, to Sep-2026) sit against electricity demand of +18.1% Apr-to-date (CEA, to Aug-2026), so billed turnover may not be keeping pace with physical output, squeezing margins.

Credit concentration: all-bank credit of Rs 832,527 Cr at a 151.1% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025) leaves little deposit cushion, so any deterioration in MSME asset quality constrains further lending to the sector.
brief.local_news: Local coverage adds a specific, dated cash-flow event beyond the data pack: AP Chambers' October 2026 representation seeking release of about ₹5,000 crore in pending MSME and food-processing incentives, noting only around ₹1,000 crore was released the previous year and that delays have hurt loan repayment and working capital. The articles also flag the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on November 12-13, 2026 as the deadline pressure point for clearing dues.
borrower_checks: Debtor days versus 90: obtain the receivables ageing and isolate government/incentive receivables, given the reported ₹5,000 crore backlog (news, Oct-2026).

GST turnover versus bank credit summations: reconcile declared GST turnover against bank statement credits for the last 12 months, in light of AP GST at -0.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% (GSTN, to Sep-2026).

Electricity bills trend versus last year: pull 12 months of power bills and compare YoY, testing whether the borrower's consumption tracks the state's +18.1% Apr-to-date and +23.0% YoY latest-month demand (CEA, to Aug-2026) or is losing share.
brief.change_the_call: A move in AP GST collections from -0.2% Apr-to-date to positive territory near India's +6.1%, or evidence that the ₹5,000 crore incentive backlog is cleared, would shift the call toward In line; a reversal of electricity demand growth below India's +9.5% would push it to Worse.

local_view.why: State GST lags India and ₹5,000 Cr incentive arrears hit MSME cash flow.

India-wide: IIP NIC 13 output +13.1% YoY. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]
India-wide: Output +11.9% Apr-to-date. [IIP, MoSPI, data to Aug-2026]

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is to lend selectively, not to the sector as a whole: GST collections rose +12.3% Apr-to-date versus India's +6.1%, and the latest month was +42.9% YoY (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), while all-bank credit of Rs 4,485 Cr grew +8.6% YoY at a 52.2% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025). Demand-side tax momentum is strong, but the low credit-deposit ratio shows banks are not yet stretching, and the news points to subsidy arrears and tourism-linked EMI stress rather than broad-based repayment capacity.
sector_risks: Payment-cycle and subsidy-delay risk: the MP's letter (news [0]) says MSME capital subsidy applications have been pending in the Directorate of Industries for over 2 years and the last subsidy was sanctioned several years ago, so borrowers' cash flows depend on a discretionary grant rather than trading receipts.

Tourism-concentration risk: news [0] states most borrowers invested in tourism, and the Port Blair airfield maintenance from March 2022 (restarting to March 2023 end) dented business, leaving loan EMIs unpaid and interest compounding.

Credit penetration lag: all-bank credit is Rs 4,485 Cr with a 52.2% credit-deposit ratio (RBI, end-Mar-2025), so a thin formal-credit base means fewer repayment histories to underwrite against, even as GST runs at +12.3% Apr-to-date (GSTN, to Sep-2026).
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The single article (news [0], dated 2026-10-12) adds a borrower-level stress signal the data pack lacks: pending MSME capital subsidy cases over 2 years, tourism-linked loan EMIs unpaid, and compounding interest after COVID-19 closures and Port Blair airfield maintenance.
borrower_checks: GST turnover versus bank credit summations: reconcile declared GST turnover against account credits for the last 12 months and flag any gap above 10%.
Debtor days versus 90: obtain the receivables ageing and confirm debtor days are at or below 90, with no subsidy receivable older than 12 months.
Electricity bills trend versus last year: compare the last 12 months of electricity bills with the prior year to confirm operating activity matches declared turnover.
brief.change_the_call: A fall in GST growth below India's +6.1% Apr-to-date, or all-bank credit growth dropping below +8.6% YoY with the credit-deposit ratio still at 52.2%, would move the call to negative.

local_view.why: GST +12.3% vs India +6.1%; latest month +42.9% YoY.

brief.verdict_rationale: The call is negative: Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band (data to Oct-2026), squeezing diesel cost share for Namakkal fleets, while Tamil Nadu GST collections fell -3.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% and -4.5% YoY in the latest month (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), signalling weaker local freight demand. Offsetting this, bank credit to transport operators is Rs 250,471 Cr outstanding, +24.6% YoY (RBI, Sep-2026), so sector leverage is expanding into a cost shock.
sector_risks: Diesel/fuel cost spike: Brent at $113/bbl (data to Oct-2026) is above the $75–100 band and scores negative, directly raising operating cost per km for Namakkal truck fleets.

Freight demand contraction: Tamil Nadu GST collections -3.2% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% and -4.5% YoY latest month (GSTN, data to Sep-2026) point to weaker goods movement and freight rates in the state.

Sand quarry closure: news reports quarries non-operational since ED investigation in Sept 2023, affecting more than 55,000 truck owners and two lakh drivers and cleaners, with owners 'struggling to repay loans' (Times of India, 2026-10-28).
brief.local_news: Limited local coverage. The only directly relevant item is the sand quarry closure report (Times of India, 2026-10-28), which states quarries have been shut since the ED probe began in Sept 2023 and that over 55,000 truck owners and two lakh drivers and cleaners are affected, with owners struggling to repay loans; the remaining articles cover the Namakkal power loom crisis, a cargo segment rather than a fleet-demand signal.
borrower_checks: Fleet utilisation: obtain monthly loaded-km per vehicle for the last 6 months and compare against the operator's own pre-closure sand-haul baseline, given the quarry shutdown reported since Sept 2023.
Diesel cost share: get fuel cost as a percentage of operating revenue per trip and stress it against Brent at $113/bbl (data to Oct-2026) versus the $75–100 band.
Customer payment days: pull receivables ageing and compute debtor days for the top 5 customers, tying to the reported loan-repayment strain among sand truck owners (Times of India, 2026-10-28).
brief.change_the_call: A move in Brent back inside the $75–100 band, or Tamil Nadu GST collections turning positive versus India's +6.1% (GSTN, data to Sep-2026), would shift the call; a further rise in Brent above $113/bbl would harden it.

local_view.why: Brent $113/bbl plus TN GST -3.2% squeeze Namakkal fleet margins and demand.
